arxiv-2211-08559.title: Robust Alzheimer’s Progression Modeling using Cross-Domain Self-Supervised Deep Learning
arxiv-2211-08559.creator: Saba Dadsetan dadsetas@gene.com, Mohsen Hejrati hejratis@gene.com, Shandong Wu shw83@pitt.edu, Somaye Hashemifar hashemifar.somaye@gene.com, for the Swedish BioFINDER study group, for the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, for the BIOCARD Study team
arxiv-2211-08559.description: Abstract Developing successful artificial intelligence systems in practice depends on both robust deep learning models and large, high-quality data. However, acquiring and labeling data can be prohibitively expensive and time-consuming in many real-world applications, such as clinical disease models. Self-supervised learning has demonstrated great potential in increasing model accuracy and robustness in small data regimes.

arxiv-2307-11492.title: Certification of randomness without seed randomness
arxiv-2307-11492.creator: Shubhayan Sarkar
arxiv-2307-11492.description: Abstract The security of any cryptographic scheme relies on access to random number generators. Device-independently certified random number generators provide maximum security as one can discard the presence of an intruder by considering only the statistics generated by these devices.

arxiv-2308-14254.title: Posterior distributions of Gibbs-type priors
arxiv-2308-14254.creator: Lancelot F. James
arxiv-2308-14254.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Lancelot F. James. Gibbs type priors have been shown to be natural generalizations of Dirichlet process (DP) priors used for intricate applications of Bayesian nonparametric methods. This includes applications to mixture models and to species sampling models arising in populations genetics. Notably these latter applications, and also applications where power law behavior such as that arising in natural language models are exhibited, provide instances where the DP model is wholly inadequate.

arxiv-2309-17351.title: Hypergraphs in LHC Phenomenology − - The Next Frontier of IRC-Safe Feature Extraction
arxiv-2309-17351.creator: Partha Konar, Vishal S. Ngairangbam, and Michael Spannowsky
arxiv-2309-17351.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Partha Konar, Vishal S. Ngairangbam, and Michael Spannowsky. In this study, we critically evaluate the approximation capabilities of existing infra-red and collinear (IRC) safe feature extraction algorithms, namely Energy Flow Networks (EFNs) and Energy-weighted Message Passing Networks (EMPNs). Our analysis reveals that these algorithms fall short in extracting features from any N N -point correlation that isn’t a power of two, based on the complete basis of IRC safe observables, specifically C-correlators.

arxiv-2310-05545.title: Janus helices: From fully attractive to hard helices
arxiv-2310-05545.creator: Laura Dal Compare, Flavio Romano, Jared A. Wood, Asaph Widmer-Cooper, Achille Giacometti
arxiv-2310-05545.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Laura Dal Compare, Flavio Romano, Jared A. Wood, Asaph Widmer-Cooper, Achille Giacometti. The phase diagram of hard helices differs from its hard rods counterpart by the presence of chiral "screw" phases stemming from the characteristic helical shape, in addition to the conventional liquid crystal phases also found for rod-like particles.

arxiv-2503-00618.title: Show Me Why It’s Correct: Saving 1/3 of Debugging Time in Program Repair with Interactive Runtime Comparison
arxiv-2503-00618.creator: Ruixin Wang, Zhongkai Zhao, Le Fang, Nan Jiang, Yiling Lou, Lin Tan, Tianyi Zhang
arxiv-2503-00618.description: Abstract . Automated Program Repair (APR) holds the promise of alleviating the burden of debugging and fixing software bugs. Despite this, developers still need to manually inspect each patch to confirm its correctness, which is tedious and time-consuming. This challenge is exacerbated in the presence of plausible patches, which accidentally pass test cases but may not correctly fix the bug.

arxiv-2506-13729.title: Algebraicity of Hodge classes on some Generalized Prym Varieties
arxiv-2506-13729.creator: Deepam Patel, Yilong Zhang
arxiv-2506-13729.description: Abstract . In this article, we revisit the construction of some algebraic cycles due to Schoen ( [ 11 ] ) on certain Prym Varieties. More precisely, we show that these cycles arise naturally from (unramified) geometric class field theory, and apply it to prove the algebraicity of certain Hodge classes on some generalized Prym Varieties .

arxiv-2510-03471.title: A Simulation Evaluation Suite for Robust Adaptive Quadcopter Control
arxiv-2510-03471.creator: Dingqi Zhang, Ran Tao, Sheng Cheng, Naira Hovakimyan, Mark W. Mueller
arxiv-2510-03471.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dingqi Zhang, Ran Tao, Sheng Cheng, Naira Hovakimyan, Mark W. Mueller. Robust adaptive control methods are essential for maintaining quadcopter performance under external disturbances and model uncertainties. However, fragmented evaluations across tasks, simulators, and implementations hinder systematic comparison of these methods. This paper introduces an easy-to-deploy, modular simulation testbed for quadcopter control, built on RotorPy , that enables evaluation under a wide range of disturbances such as wind, payload shifts, rotor faults, and control latency.

pmc-11353515.title: Probabilistic Estimation and Control of Dynamical Systems Using Particle Filter with Adaptive Backward Sampling
pmc-11353515.creator: Taketo Omi, Toshiaki Omori, Carlos Dias Maciel
pmc-11353515.description: Estimating and controlling dynamical systems from observable time-series data are essential for understanding and manipulating nonlinear dynamics. This paper proposes a probabilistic framework for simultaneously estimating and controlling nonlinear dynamics under noisy observation conditions. Our proposed method utilizes the particle filter not only as a state estimator and a prior estimator for the dynamics but also as a controller.

pmc-11673464.title: Development and biochemical characterization of freeze‐dried guava powder fortified with Lactobacillus plantarum
pmc-11673464.creator: Ali Asad Yousaf, Hui Zeng, Kashif Sarfraz Abbasi, Teresa Bergholz, Muhammad Siddiq, Kirk Dolan
pmc-11673464.description: Guava (Psidium guajava L.) is one of the most nutrient‐dense fruits, which is native to tropical and subtropical regions of the world. The processing of value‐added products from guava has not been carried out on a scale similar to some other fruits, which offers an opportunity to fully exploit the potential of this fruit, such as guava‐based nutraceutical food products.

pmc-12808777.title: Enhancing rapeseed germination by nano zinc oxide and zinc sulfate particles under interrupted irrigation
pmc-12808777.creator: Seyed Davood Alavifard, Mansour Taghvaei, Ruhollah Naderi, Mohsen Edalat, Bahram Heidari, Beata Dedicova

pmc-13462329.title: Continuous nonthermal slab gap formed by progressive tearing beneath Northeast Asia
pmc-13462329.creator: Jung-Hun Song, Seongryong Kim, Benoît Tauzin, Junkee Rhie
pmc-13462329.description: Slab gaps in subducted plates are widely hypothesized to channel hot mantle upwellings, yet their formation and thermal state remain enigmatic. Here we image a continuous ~1000 km-long arcuate slab gap in the mantle transition zone beneath Northeast Asia with no evidence of anomalous heat.

pmc-13700306.title: Targeting MRPL37 disrupts the pro-tumorigenic mitochondrial cascade in bladder cancer: from LRPPRC deficiency to ROS/AKT axis inhibition
pmc-13700306.creator: Xieyuan Leng, Wenhao Lu, Rongbin Zhou, Chengbang Wang, Zuheng Wang, Haodong Peng, Yitong Guo, Baoyu Huang, Dongwei Pan, Dianyu Wang, Zequn Su, Xuanfan Liu, Xuefang Liang, Tian Guo, Wen Liang, Wentin Chen, Zihang Huang, Zhe Chen, Yigan Zhang, Fubo Wang
pmc-13700306.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bladder cancer (BLCA) is a urinary system malignant tumor with high morbidity and mortality worldwide. There is an urgent need for new biomarkers and therapeutic targets. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing, MitoCarta database and the Cancer Genome Atlas data, this study found that mitochondrial ribosomal protein L37 (MRPL37) was significantly up-regulated in BLCA, and its expression level was related to disease progression and poor prognosis.
